crisis.label: Severe
crisis.detail: Jul 30: US-Iran pause breaks after 5 days - Iran's IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan in an attempted surprise attack (~5:45pm ET Jul 28); CENTCOM confirmed all missiles intercepted, no casualties or damage (CNBC/Al Jazeera, Jul 29). US and Saudi aircraft retaliated with strikes on Iran-backed militia logistics and weapons sites across seven Iraqi provinces, the first announced Saudi participation in offensive strikes of the war (NPR/PBS, Jul 29); Iraqi sources report 20+ Popular Mobilization Forces fighters killed. Trump told Fox News Iran 'is going to get a beating.' Brent $89.46, up from Jul 29's $86.81 close after trading as high as $90.74 intraday Wednesday (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, CNBC); Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial tanker traffic with zero tanker crossings Jul 27 (Windward); tail raised to 60%

topAlert: JUL 30: Pause breaks - Iran missile attack on US Jordan base intercepted; US/Saudi retaliate in Iraq, first Saudi offensive strikes of war; Trump vows 'beating'; Brent $89.46, up from $86.81 close
commodityScenario: Jul 30: The five-day US-Iran pause (Jul 25-29) broke after Iran's IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan in an attempted surprise attack around 5:45pm ET Jul 28; CENTCOM confirmed all missiles intercepted with no casualties or damage (CNBC/Al Jazeera, Jul 29). Within hours, US and Saudi aircraft struck IRGC-directed logistics and weapons sites across seven Iraqi provinces in retaliation for more than 30 drone attacks in 72 hours; Iraqi sources reported over 20 Popular Mobilization Forces fighters killed - the first announced Saudi participation in offensive strikes of the war (NPR/PBS, Jul 29). Trump told Fox News Iran 'is going to get a beating.' Brent rose to $89.46 (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 30), up from Jul 29's $86.81 close, after trading as high as $90.74 intraday Wednesday (CNBC); note Yahoo's own -7.56% session-change figure appears to reference a stale prior close and should not be read as the day's direction. TTF ticked up to 60.35 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance TTF=F, Jul 29). Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial tanker traffic - Windward reported just 6 total transits and zero tanker crossings on Jul 27. Tail raised to 60% as the pause and diplomatic track have collapsed.
marketContext: Pause breaks after Iran missile attack on US Jordan base (intercepted, no casualties); US/Saudi retaliate in Iraq - first Saudi offensive strikes of the war; Trump vows 'beating'; Brent $89.46, up from $86.81 close (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 30); Hormuz effectively closed, zero tanker crossings Jul 27 (Windward); tail 60%.

todaysEvents.summary: US, Saudi strike Iran proxies in Iraq
todaysEvents.delta: Up: US and Saudi aircraft struck Iran-backed militia sites across seven Iraqi provinces, retaliating for 30+ drone attacks in 72 hours; 20+ militia fighters reported killed. First announced Saudi offensive strikes of the war. Sources: NPR, PBS, Jul 29.

todaysEvents.summary: Trump vows retaliation as Brent surges
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Trump told Fox News Iran 'is going to get a beating,' vowing to hit Iran hard. Brent traded as high as $90.74 intraday Wednesday before easing to $89.46, up from Jul 29's $86.81 close (Yahoo Finance BZ=F, Jul 30; CNBC). Sources: CNBC, Jul 29.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: The Omani-led diplomatic channel resumes traction after this shock is absorbed without further widening. Indirect Iran-US contact via Oman eventually produces a framework for phased Hormuz reopening. Brent settles toward $80-90/bbl as the risk premium partially deflates. Probability cut from 25% to 10% given the pause has now broken with a direct Iranian attack on US forces and broadened US-Saudi retaliation.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The current retaliatory exchange stays roughly contained to proxy targets (Iraq militias) rather than direct strikes on Iranian soil or Saudi energy infrastructure. Hormuz remains constrained with minimal tanker transits. Brent trades $90-110/bbl, TTF stays elevated. Probability held near prior level at 30% given the exchange has so far avoided direct Iran-Saudi energy infrastructure hits.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The pause has broken and US strikes resume at scale, potentially targeting nuclear sites, with Iran escalating to full-scale offensive operations; Saudi Arabia's first offensive strikes convert it from target to active belligerent, raising the risk of direct retaliation against Saudi energy infrastructure. Brent spikes $100-140+/bbl, JKM above $30/MMBtu. Probability raised from 40% to 60% reflecting the collapsed pause, Iran's direct attack on US forces, and Saudi Arabia's entry as a combatant.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $86.81 (Jul 29, -13.78% from peak, Yahoo Finance BZ=F) as the US-Iran pause held for a 5th day -> $89.46 (Jul 30, Yahoo Finance BZ=F), up from Jul 29's close, after Iran's missile attack on a US base in Jordan broke the pause and Trump vowed retaliation; Brent traded as high as $90.74 intraday Wednesday (CNBC). Working range raised to $80-95 base; $90-110 stress; $110-140+ tail.
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.93/MMBtu (Jul 16, Trading Economics) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Trading Economics/Reuters Sept-delivery assessment, +0.80%) as 13 nights of US strikes and sustained Hormuz closure tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $21.43/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Jul 29). Qatar force majeure extended to mid-September (Reuters, Jul 23; AGBI, confirmed into a fourth month). Ras Laffan restart not before late Aug 2026.
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> 63.58/MWh (Jul 24, +2.71% vs Jul 23, MacroMicro) -> 56.50/MWh (Jul 28, -8.72% from Jul 27, Yahoo Finance TTF=F) as the pause held -> 60.35/MWh (Jul 29, +6.8% vs Jul 28, Yahoo Finance TTF=F) as the pause broke and the risk premium returned. Still elevated on persistent LNG supply disruption from Qatar force majeure.
priceNarratives.Credit: iTraxx Asia IG est. ~145bp (Jul 30, +7bp); ASEAN HY est. ~492bp (+14bp) as the US-Iran pause broke after Iran's missile attack on US forces in Jordan and Trump vowed retaliation, reversing prior de-escalation in Asian risk sentiment. Tail raised to 60% (from 40%) on the collapsed pause and Saudi Arabia's entry as an active belligerent.
